memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Isaac's servants dug in the valley and discovered a well of fresh water there. But the herders of Gerar quarreled with those of Isaac and said, 'The water is ours!' So he named the well Esek, because they disputed with him. Then they dug another well, but they quarreled over that one also; so he named it Sitnah. He moved on from there and dug another well, and no one quarreled over it. He named it Rehoboth, saying, 'Now the LORD has given us room and we will flourish in the land.'" - Gen 26:19-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Isaac's servants dig a well and find fresh water — but the local herders claim it as theirs. So Isaac names it Esek ("dispute") and moves on. They dig again; again there is a quarrel, and he names that one Sitnah ("opposition"). Still Isaac does not fight. He moves once more, digs again, and this time no one argues. He names it Rehoboth, saying, "Now the LORD has given us room."

What patience and faith! Twice Isaac gave up wells rather than quarrel, trusting that God would eventually make space for him. And God did. Rehoboth means "room" or "wide places" — a testimony that God had gone ahead and provided.

Sometimes the path to God's blessing runs through Esek and Sitnah before it reaches Rehoboth. We face disputes and opposition, and we are tempted to quit or to fight bitterly. But Isaac shows a better way: keep doing what is right, keep trusting God, and keep moving forward peaceably. In His time, God opens up room to flourish.

If you are in a season of Esek and Sitnah — one conflict after another — do not lose heart. Keep digging faithfully. Your Rehoboth may be just one more well away.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I in an "Esek" or "Sitnah" season of repeated opposition?
2. Can I keep trusting God to make room rather than fighting bitterly?
3. Where do I need to keep "digging" faithfully and wait for God's Rehoboth?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, in seasons of dispute and opposition, give me a patient, trusting heart. Thank You that in Your time You make room for Your people to flourish. Amen.
